clue.text: Small child loves position as pupil down under

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
love is zero in tennis, and a zero looks like the letter O, so two loves give OO
the lie of something is its position, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: A little one who adores being a pupil in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' is the informal name for Australia, where this is slang for a schoolchild.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a schoolchild, especially a school-leaver, so it names a pupil in that country.

clue.text: Prim celebrity introduces Charlie and Henry

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet
Hy is an old abbreviation for the name Henry

explanation.surface: A prudish famous person brings in two men called Charlie and Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff and formal in manner, like a starched collar, hence prudish or prim.

clue.text: In this place consumes curry I left, needing a drink

indicators.note: consuming takes something inside, so the word for curry goes within the other

parts.note: here means in this place

indicators.note: left means gone away, so the I is removed

parts.note: a balti is a kind of curry

explanation.surface: Somebody eats most of a curry here and then needs something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of herbs in hot water is a beverage.

clue.text: Cycle part men put at front

indicators.note: put at front means this piece goes before the other

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers, i.e. men
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: Bike components get placed ahead by men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' suggests a bicycle; it means one circuit round a path.
explanation.definitionFit: One complete revolution round a path, as a planet makes, is a circuit or cycle.

clue.text: I'll introduce solvers from different countries: roll up!

parts.note: Interpol is the international police organisation whose detectives solve crimes across borders

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a rota is a roll or list of duties

explanation.surface: An announcer introduces crossword solvers from many nations and invites them in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solvers' points at puzzlers; the detectives meant solve crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: One who interpolates inserts or introduces material into something, so would say this of itself.

clue.text: Boat fit to be used in war, gutted

indicators.note: one piece is put to use inside another, so the fit word goes within the other letters
gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters of the word war

parts.note: hale means fit and healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A vessel fit for wartime service, though it has been stripped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boat' is the definition, not the war vessel of the surface: gutting a word removes all its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaling ship, or a whaleboat, is a kind of vessel, so it fits the general word boat.

clue.text: Hot songs on piano before light musical

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
airs are songs or tunes
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Racy numbers on the piano before a light-hearted show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light musical' reads as a frothy show, but 'light' is a beam; the musical is Hairspray.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage show set in 1960s Baltimore, later filmed, that is a well-known musical.

clue.text: It's OK to run away

definitions.meaning: describes something above board, lawful or genuine
informal British phrase for fleeing on foot

explanation.surface: Permission granted to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for lawful or genuine, and split into two it is British slang for fleeing.

clue.text: Wolf Hall actor having lines cut

parts.note: RY, railway, is a set of lines
to lance is to cut, as with a boil

explanation.surface: An actor in a historical drama gets some of his lines cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Rylance played Thomas Cromwell in the BBC's Wolf Hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Rylance starred as Thomas Cromwell in the 2015 television adaptation of Wolf Hall.

clue.text: Versatile performers replaced mostly bad actors

indicators.note: the letters are put back in different places, so they are rearranged
mostly means all but a bit, so the word bad loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Talented performers have taken the place of most of the poor actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts bad to BA; 'replaced' rearranges BA with ACTORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Circus tumblers and trapeze artists are performers whose skills are notably flexible and varied.

clue.text: Caveman following girl beyond home

indicators.note: one piece comes beyond, that is after, the other in the answer

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
to be in is to be at home
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A prehistoric man chasing a girl a long way from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caveman' is not a prehistoric man: it is the legendary hero after whom Fingal's Cave on the Scottish island of Staffa is named.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ossianic hero gives his name to a famous sea cave, so he is playfully the man of the cave.

clue.text: Theatrical dame tucked into cooked sardine? That's potty

indicators.note: one piece is tucked into another, so the dame goes inside the other letters
something cooked has been changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Dame Judi Dench is the famous stage actress

explanation.surface: An actress digs into a cooked fish dinner, which seems crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' looks like crazy; it is pottery, a playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain from the Meissen factory near Dresden is fine pottery, hence playfully potty.

clue.text: One talks a lot about top designer meeting the Queen

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
a hatter designs hats, which are worn on top
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A chatty person going on about a leading designer meeting the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top designer' looks like a fashion star; it is someone who makes toppers, i.e. hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who chatters is by nature a person who talks constantly and at length.

clue.text: Locatin' protest

definitions.meaning: locating means placing or siting, and the apostrophe drops the final g as in casual speech
a demonstration where people occupy a building and refuse to leave

explanation.surface: A casual, g-dropping word for finding a place, followed by a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe signals the dropped G, as in casual speech: locatin' for locating.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a demonstration in which people occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: Gaps regularly appearing in my teeth even now

indicators.note: regular gaps mean every other letter is skipped, so the remaining alternate letters are taken from my teeth

explanation.surface: Someone notices gaps showing up at intervals in their teeth even now.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb meaning still or so far, it matches even now, as in 'not finished yet'.

clue.text: More covers I ordered, as part of this?

definitions.text: More covers I ordered, as part of this?

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A hotel guest asks for extra bedding as part of a delivery to the room.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is a guest ordering more covers (bedding or dishes) through the hotel's delivery to the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels deliver meals and extras to guests' bedrooms, so extra covers ordered would be part of it.

clue.text: Poor cafés should be refurbished: that's the view from on high

indicators.note: refurbished means done up and remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Run-down cafés need doing up, says someone looking down on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene of rooftops seen from above is the panorama looking down from height.

clue.text: Balsam perhaps formed by sap in time

indicators.note: the answer is formed by rearranging the following letters

explanation.surface: A resin formed in time from sap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balsam' suggests a resin from sap; it is the flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy Lizzie and garden balsam belong to this plant genus, so balsam is an example.

clue.text: In Cambridgeshire location, Socialists together speak out in detailed fashion

indicators.note: the following pieces sit in the place name, enclosed by its letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: together joins the party with the next piece side by side

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, Britain's socialist party
to orate is to speak out formally, make a speech

explanation.surface: In a Fenland town, left-wingers jointly voice their views at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small city in Cambridgeshire, England; LAB is the usual short form of the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Done with great care over every detail, intricately, as an elaborately carved screen.

clue.text: Old saintly cardinal possibly ran out

parts.note: ex means former or old
pi is short for pious, saintly
cardinal is a shade of red, from the cardinals' robes

explanation.surface: An elderly holy churchman may have died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' seems a churchman; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whose term has ended, like a passport, has lapsed or come to an end.

clue.text: Turned up first for beer … here?

definitions.text: Turned up first for beer … here?

indicators.note: turned means the word up is turned round and read backwards
first for means take the opening letter of the word beer

explanation.surface: Someone arrives early at the place they get a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, it is where you turn up first for a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A British public house is the place people go to drink beer, so it is the 'here' of the clue.

clue.text: British entrepreneur in a pickle, short of time

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: Branston is a well-known British brand of pickle

explanation.surface: A British businessman is in trouble and running out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a pickle' reads as in trouble; Branston is a British relish brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Richard Branson founded the Virgin group, a famous British business magnate.

clue.text: Attendants providing sheets

definitions.meaning: young servants or attendants, such as those at a wedding or at court
leaves of paper in a book

explanation.surface: Servants supplying bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both boy servants at court or weddings and the leaves of a book.

clue.text: Unidentified item shown by US army medic?

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers, the US army
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A strange object displayed by an American army doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a gadget or thingamajig whose name one does not know.

clue.text: Musicians endlessly fired by return of cultural activities

indicators.note: without its ends, the synonym of fired loses its first and last letters

parts.note: torched means set fire to

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the word for cultural activities is read backwards

parts.note: the arts are cultural activities

explanation.surface: Musicians sacked without end because the arts are coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims TORCHED to ORCHE; 'return of' turns ARTS into STRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ensemble of instrumental players is a body of musicians.

clue.text: Church official partly covered lectern over

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, read backwards
partly means only some of the letters inside covered lectern are taken

explanation.surface: A cleric partly draped the reading desk.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian and other churches, a lay officer who helps govern the congregation.

clue.text: Rogue artist's name ultimately forgotten

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist, and the 's gives RAS

indicators.note: the final letter is left off the word for name

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A rogue painter's name is eventually forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous scoundrel, the sort of rogue who is dishonest or cheeky.

clue.text: Without thinking, deputy lieutenant probes explosive near ship

indicators.note: the deputy probes, that is, pokes into, the explosive word

parts.note: a mine is an explosive device
DL is the abbreviation for Deputy Lieutenant, a county officer in Britain
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An officer recklessly investigates a bomb near a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A Deputy Lieutenant (DL) is a British county officer assisting the Lord Lieutenant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without thought or care is acting senselessly, without using the mind.

clue.text: Stockholder maybe right to invest in Channel port

indicators.note: investing in something puts money inside it, so the letter goes inside the port

parts.note: Dover is the English port on the Channel

explanation.surface: A shareholder may be right to put money into a ferry port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stockholder' suggests shares; here it is someone who holds livestock, driving cattle to market.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover herds cattle or sheep, so he literally holds stock, the farming sense of livestock.

clue.text: Former Beatle is performing after Prince's brief appearance

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the shortened name
brief means cut short, so the prince's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Harry is the British prince
on means performing, as an act on stage

explanation.surface: An ex-Beatle is on stage after a royal's short cameo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearance' just completes the surface. George Harrison was the Beatles' lead guitarist.
explanation.definitionFit: George Harrison played guitar in the Beatles, the group that broke up in 1970.
